issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies the attribute `numberOfTutors` as type `int`, but the solution declares it as `short`. This creates a cross-artifact mismatch for the same field and can cause confusion and failing tests if students implement `int` as specified.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution field declaration to `private int numberOfTutors;` and adjust any dependent signatures/logic to use `int` consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the constructor to initialize all attributes as defined in the UML (where `numberOfTutors` is `int`), but the solution constructor uses `short numberOfTutors`. This makes the constructor signature inconsistent with the specified model and can break tests expecting an `int` parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the solution constructor signature to use `int numberOfTutors` (keeping the UML order) and assign it to an `int` field.

issues.description: The solution setter `setNumberOfTutors` takes a `short`, while the UML/problem statement specifies `numberOfTutors` as an `int`. This makes the setter signature inconsistent with the specified attribute type and can cause test failures if an `int` setter is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Change `setNumberOfTutors(short numberOfTutors)` to `setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors)` after updating the field to `int`.
